entries.title: Chat and Learn can say when the article is out of date
entries.body: Chat, Learn's Recall and Tutorial, and Quiz feedback may add one short, separate note when a checkable fact in the article is wrong or out of date, or when a settled consensus or a live dispute bears on one of its central claims. Each note says where it comes from: the article, the AI's own knowledge, or the web. It is about the piece, not about you, and never counts against your own reading of it.

entries.title: On a touchscreen, links within the article ask first
entries.body: Tapping an underlined phrase that points to another passage in the article shows its card first, with "Tap again to go there"; a second tap takes you. A mouse click still goes straight there. The "back to …" button that appears after a jump fades after 30 seconds, unless you are pointing at it.

entries.title: Paragraph icons give the text more room on phones
entries.body: On a phone, the column of icons to the right of each paragraph shrinks to a thin strip showing only its marks and the line that shows your reading time, so the text gets a little more width. Tap a paragraph and its controls appear as a row above its top-right corner. Larger screens are unchanged.

entries.title: The More button sits after Skim
entries.body: On the bar of mode buttons at the bottom of the page, More has moved one place along, from after Summary to after Skim. On a narrow phone, where that place would be off the edge of the screen, More comes first instead.

entries.title: Glossary's note on a new list is tucked away
entries.body: In the Glossary panel, the explanation under "Write a new list" has moved behind a small information button beside it. Point at it or press it to read it; otherwise it takes up no space.

entries.title: Poems quoted in a PDF keep their line breaks
entries.body: When a PDF quoted verse, its lines ran together into a single paragraph. They now keep the author's line breaks, for quotes of four lines or more in PDFs added from here on. Short quotes and ordinary paragraphs look as they did.
